ties.applies_to: governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, state auditor, state treasurer or attorney general, in a general election
ties.steps: the secretary of state issues a proclamation stating the tie; the general assembly, by joint vote and without delay at its next regular session, chooses one of the tied persons; the speaker of the house files a certificate with the secretary of state declaring who is elected
ties.who: the general assembly, by joint vote of both houses

sources.quote: If two or more persons receive an equal number of votes for election to the office of governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, state auditor, state treasurer or attorney general, and a higher number of votes than any other candidate for the same office, the secretary of state shall, immediately after the results of the election have been announced, issue a proclamation stating the fact, and the general assembly shall, by joint vote and without delay at its next regular session, choose one of such persons for the office.
The speaker of the house shall file a certificate declaring which person has been elected to the office with the secretary of state.

ties.note: RSMo 115.517.1. Subsection 4 (next rules) lets the tied candidates agree to a drawing of lots instead. The Missouri Constitution was not read for its own words on the governor.

ties.applies_to: federal office (U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative), state senator, state representative, and a circuit judge not subject to Article V, section 25 of the Constitution, in a general election
ties.steps: the governor issues a proclamation stating the tie and ordering a special election, to determine which candidate is elected; only the names of the persons who tied for the highest vote appear on the special election ballot; the special election is conducted and the votes counted as in other elections
ties.who: the governor orders it; the election authorities conduct it

sources.quote: If two or more persons receive an equal number of votes for election to federal office, state senator, state representative or circuit judge not subject to the provisions of Article V, Section 25 of the State Constitution, and a higher number of votes than any other candidate for the same office, the governor shall, immediately after the results of the election have been announced, issue a proclamation stating the fact and ordering a special election to determine which candidate is elected to the office.

Only the names of those persons who have received an equal number of votes for nomination or election to an office at any other election, and a higher number of votes than any other candidate for the same office at the same election shall appear on the special election ballot.

ties.note: RSMo 115.517.2 and 115.519. The statute calls it a special election; its section 115.519 is headed 'Runoff election between tied candidates only'. The tied candidates may instead agree to a drawing of lots (below). Presidential electors are not in this subsection; chapter 128 has its own rule (below). A seat in the state senate or house is also judged by that chamber in a contest (115.563).

ties.applies_to: any office not named in 115.515 or 115.517.1 and .2 (read as county, municipal and other local offices), in a general election
ties.steps: the officer with whom the tied candidates filed their declarations of candidacy issues a proclamation stating the tie and ordering a special election among the tied candidates only; the election is conducted and the votes counted as in other elections
ties.who: the officer with whom the candidates filed their declarations of candidacy

sources.quote: If two or more persons receive an equal number of votes for nomination or election to any office not otherwise provided for in section 115.515 or this section, and a higher number of votes than any other candidate for nomination or election to the same office, the officer with whom such candidates filed their declarations of candidacy shall, immediately after the results of the election have been certified, issue a proclamation stating the fact and ordering a special election to determine which candidate is elected to the office.

ties.note: RSMo 115.517.3. The text says 'any office not otherwise provided for', not 'local'; that this is the rule for county, municipal and school offices is my reading [inferred]. A charter of a city may differ and was not read.

ties.applies_to: any tied election, if all the tied candidates agree to the alternative
ties.steps: as an alternative to the special election (or the vote of the general assembly), if the tied candidates agree, the officer with whom they filed may, after notifying each candidate of the time and place at least five days before, determine the winner by lot; any tied candidate may decline to have his or her name put into the drawing
ties.who: the officer with whom the tied candidates filed their declarations of candidacy

sources.quote: As an alternative to the procedure prescribed in subsections 1, 2, and 3 of this section, if the candidates who received an equal number of votes in such election agree to the procedure prescribed in this subsection, the officer with whom such candidates filed their declarations of candidacy may, after notification of the time and place of such drawing given to each such candidate at least five days before such drawing, determine the winner of such election by lot.

As an alternative to the procedure prescribed in subsections 1 and 2 of this section, if the candidates who received an equal number of votes in such election agree to the procedure prescribed in this subsection, the officer with whom such candidates filed their declarations of candidacy may, after notification of the time and place of such drawing given to each such candidate at least five days before such drawing, determine the winner of such election by lot.

ties.note: RSMo 115.517.4 (general elections) and 115.515.3 (party primaries). It needs the agreement of the tied candidates; a refusal by one sends the race to the main rule for its office.

ties.applies_to: presidential electors, in the general election
ties.steps: the governor notifies the general assembly of the tie, and the election is determined by joint vote of both houses, which choose one of the persons with equal votes
ties.who: the general assembly, by joint vote of both houses

sources.quote: If two or more persons residing in one district shall have an equal number of votes given in the state, as aforesaid, and more than any other person residing in the same district, the governor shall immediately notify the general assembly thereof, and such election shall be determined by joint vote of both houses of the general assembly, by choosing one of the persons so having an equal number of votes.

ties.note: RSMo 128.080, in its 1939 text, which speaks of persons 'residing in one district'; how it reads for electors chosen by the whole state today is not decided here. Whether the 115.517 alternative of lots (which names no electors) can be used was not read.

ties.applies_to: a party primary for nomination (federal office, governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, attorney general, treasurer, auditor, circuit judge, state senator, state representative, and all other offices except party committeeman or committeewoman)
ties.steps: for the offices in the first list the governor, and for other offices the officer with whom the candidates filed, issues a proclamation stating the tie and ordering a special primary election among the tied candidates only, held not less than fourteen nor more than thirty days after the proclamation, conducted as other primaries
ties.who: the governor, or the officer with whom the candidates filed their declarations of candidacy

sources.quote: If two or more persons receive an equal number of votes for nomination as a party's candidate for any federal office, governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, attorney general, state treasurer, state auditor, circuit judge [...] the governor shall, immediately after the results of the election have been announced, issue a proclamation stating the fact and ordering a special primary election to determine the party's nominee for the office.
The proclamation shall set the date of the election, which shall be not less than fourteen or more than thirty days after the proclamation is issued

Only the names of those persons who have received an equal number of votes for nomination to an office at party primary and a higher number of votes than any other candidate for the same office on the same party ballot shall appear on the special primary election ballot.

ties.note: RSMo 115.515 and 115.519. The tied candidates may agree to a drawing of lots instead (115.515.3, recorded above). For party committeeman and committeewoman, 115.613 has its own tie clause, not read.

ties.applies_to: a tie vote on a ballot question
ties.steps: no provision for a tie on a ballot question was found
ties.note: Read: RSMo 115.515, 115.517, 115.519 (each speaks of candidates and offices only), 115.553 and 115.577 (contests of a question), and the titles of every section of chapter 115 in the table of contents; the only title with 'tie' besides 115.515 and 115.517 is 115.613 (party committee). The Missouri Constitution (initiative and referendum, Article III) was not read.

recounts.election: primary or general election, where the candidate filed, or the question was filed, with the secretary of state

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast (for a question, the votes cast on the question)
threshold.conditions: the request must state that the person, or the person's position on a question, was defeated by less than one-half of one percent of the votes cast
threshold.in_words: a candidate who filed with the secretary of state, or a person whose position on a statewide question lost, by less than one-half of one percent of the votes cast, is allowed a recount on filing a request with the secretary of state

who_may_request: the defeated candidate, or the person whose position on a question was defeated, by a request filed with the secretary of state not later than seven days after certification of the election

sources.quote: the defeated candidate or the person whose position on a question was defeated by less than one-half of one percent of the votes cast on the question shall be allowed a recount pursuant to this section by filing with the secretary of state a request for a recount stating that the person or the person's position on a question was defeated by less than one-half of one percent of the votes cast.
Such request shall be filed not later than seven days after certification of the election.
The secretary of state shall conduct and certify the results of the recount as the official results in the election within twenty days of receipt of the aforementioned notice of recount.
or for recount other than the automatic recount provided for in section 115.601

recounts.note: RSMo 115.601.3 and .4. The secretary of state runs it with persons appointed equally from lists of the contestant and the opponent; 'recount' is defined as one additional counting of all votes counted for the office or on the question. Subsection 1 of the same section says 'less than one percent', the heading says 'one-half of one percent', and subsection 3 says 'one-half of one percent' for these filers; the subsection that governs these filers is 3, so 0.5 is recorded. Section 115.575(1) calls this 'the automatic recount', but 115.601.3 requires a filed request, so it is recorded as requested. Which offices file with the secretary of state is not stated in the sections read (115.349 says 'the appropriate election official'); the kinds listed are my reading from the offices whose abstracts go to the secretary of state (115.507.4) [inferred].

recounts.election: primary or other election, where the candidate filed, or the question was filed, with a local election authority

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast for the office (or on the question)
threshold.conditions: the recount is requested through an election contest (a petition to the circuit court) and conducted under the direction of the court; for an office with two or more seats, the second-highest candidate who lost by less than one percent also has the right
threshold.in_words: a contestant defeated by less than one percent of the votes cast, or a person whose position on a question was defeated by less than one percent, has the right to a recount, requested by the contest petition and conducted under the court

who_may_request: a contestant in a primary or other election contest (a candidate on the ballot, or one or more registered voters of the area for a question), by a verified petition: not later than five days after the official announcement for a primary, not later than thirty days after it for other elections
recounts.cost_bearer: the contestant may be required to post a bond for the costs and expenses; the court may adjudge the costs, including the cost of a recount, against the unsuccessful party

sources.quote: Any contestant in a primary or other election contest who was defeated by less than one percent of the votes cast for the office and any contestant who received the second highest number of votes cast for that office if two or more are to be elected and who was defeated by less than one percent of the votes cast, or any person whose position on a question was defeated by less than one percent of the votes cast on the question, shall have the right to a recount of the votes cast for the office or on the question.

such recount shall be requested in accordance with the provisions of section 115.531 or 115.577 and conducted under the direction of the court or the commissioner representing the court trying the contest

Not later than five days after the official announcement of the results of a primary election is issued by the election authority or the secretary of state, as the case may be, any candidate desiring to contest the primary election shall file a verified petition in the office of the clerk of the circuit court

Not later than thirty days after the official announcement of the election result by the election authority, any person authorized by section 115.553 who wishes to contest the election for any office or on any question provided in section 115.575 shall file a verified petition in the office of the clerk of the appropriate circuit court.

The costs and expenses of any election contest, including the cost and expense of a recount, may be adjudged against the unsuccessful party with payment of the costs and expenses enforceable as in civil cases.

recounts.note: RSMo 115.601.1 and .2, 115.531, 115.577, 115.591. 115.585 sets how the court conducts a recount (a writ to each election authority, who set a day within twenty days; paper ballots opened and counted, machine counters read, ballot cards retested and recounted automatically or by hand). That local filers are the ones with the one-percent route, and the secretary-of-state filers the half-percent route, is the section's own division in subsections 2 and 3; the kinds listed are my reading [inferred].

recounts.election: general or special election under contest

threshold.conditions: a prima facie showing of irregularities which place the result in doubt; a prima facie case is made where the validity of a number of votes equal to or greater than the margin of defeat is placed in doubt
threshold.in_words: no margin is required; the court (or, for a state senator or representative, the chamber, or, for the six state officers and statewide questions, the supreme court) must order a recount of the votes brought in question if irregularities place the result in doubt

who_may_request: any candidate for the office (who may challenge the correctness of the returns), or one or more registered voters of the area for a question, by a verified petition not later than thirty days after the official announcement
recounts.cost_bearer: the contestant may be required to post bond; costs and the cost of a recount may be adjudged against the unsuccessful party

sources.quote: If the court or legislative body hearing a contest finds there is a prima facie showing of irregularities which place the result of any contested election in doubt, the court or legislative body shall order a recount of all votes brought in question by the petition or its answer.
Where the issue is drawn over the validity of certain votes cast, a prima facie case is made if the validity of a number of votes equal to or greater than the margin of defeat is placed in doubt.
Any candidate for election to any office may challenge the correctness of the returns for the office, charging that irregularities occurred in the election.
All contested elections for the office of governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, attorney general, state treasurer and state auditor shall be heard and determined by the supreme court.

All contested elections for the office of state senator shall be heard and determined by the state senate. All contested elections for the office of state representative shall be heard and determined by the state house of representatives.

Not later than thirty days after the official announcement of the election result by the secretary of state, any person authorized by section 115.553 who wishes to contest the election for any office or on any question provided in section 115.555 , shall file a verified petition in the office of the clerk of the supreme court.

recounts.note: RSMo 115.583 with 115.553, 115.555, 115.557, 115.563, 115.575, 115.577. Other contests are heard by the circuit court chosen by the contestant (115.575.2). The text of 115.557 prints a space before the comma ('115.555 , shall file').

threshold.conditions: a prima facie showing of irregularities which place the result of the primary in doubt; the same test of 'a number of votes equal to or greater than the margin of defeat' applies
threshold.in_words: no margin is required; the circuit court must order a recount of the votes brought in question if irregularities place the primary result in doubt

who_may_request: any candidate desiring to contest the primary, by a verified petition filed not later than five days after the official announcement of the results
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read for a primary (115.591, on costs, speaks of 'the court or legislative body' in 'each case of a contested election'; the primary bond is in 115.547, not read)

sources.quote: If the court finds there is a prima facie showing of irregularities which place the result of the primary election in doubt, the court shall order a recount of all votes brought in question by the petition or its answer.

any candidate desiring to contest the primary election shall file a verified petition in the office of the clerk of the circuit court of any circuit in which part of the election was held and in which any alleged irregularity occurred

recounts.note: RSMo 115.539 and 115.531. The sections on how a primary recount is conducted (115.541, 115.543) and the primary bond (115.547) were not read.

recounts.election: any election in which the election authority finds errors

threshold.conditions: the election authority is convinced that errors of omission or commission occurred on the part of the election authority, election judges or election personnel; the court may order a new election only if the irregularities were sufficient to cast doubt on the outcome
threshold.in_words: no margin; the election authority may petition the circuit court for a recount or a new election

sources.quote: The election authority, if convinced that errors of omission or commission have occurred on the part of the election authority, election judges, or any election personnel in the conduct of an election, may petition the circuit court for a recount or a new election and the court is authorized to order a new election if the evidence provided demonstrates that the irregularities were sufficient to cast doubt on the outcome of the election.

recounts.note: RSMo 115.600. The election authority is the county clerk or board of election commissioners; the section's own annotation (Knipp) limits the board to a petition for a recount, which this page prints but which is a court case, not law, and was not relied on.

recounts.election: general election of presidential electors under contest

threshold.in_words: no margin and no recount by name; a contest of the election of an elector is decided by a joint vote of both houses of the general assembly, on a petition to it, with a joint committee taking the testimony

who_may_request: any person contesting the election of an elector, by a petition to the general assembly

sources.quote: All contested elections for electors shall be determined by a joint vote of both houses of the general assembly.

recounts.note: RSMo 128.100. Whether the 115.601 recount applies to electors was not decided from the sections read.

unread.what: RSMo 115.537, 115.541, 115.543, 115.547 (how a primary recount is conducted, its bond), 115.613 (party committee tie), the Missouri Constitution (governor, Article IV; initiative, Article III) and local charters

notes: All sections were read one at a time at the Revisor of Statutes' site (revisor.mo.gov); no refusal. One fetch of a section number that does not exist (115.602, tried as a neighbour of 115.601) returned the site's own page 'Trying to access pages that don't exist will be directed here' with the line 'Speeding: 0'; it was not a refusal, no further numbers were guessed, and the sections after it were taken from the chapter's table of contents.

Missouri has no recount without a request, a contest or a petition by the election authority. The one margin rule is RSMo 115.601: one-half of one percent for those who filed with the secretary of state, to be requested within seven days after certification; one percent for a contestant whose contest is heard by a court. Section 115.575(1) nonetheless calls the 115.601 recount 'automatic'.

A tie is settled by a special election among the tied candidates only (the governor orders it for federal and state legislative offices, the officer with whom they filed for the rest), or by the general assembly for the six state officers and for electors, or by lot if every tied candidate agrees.
